races.name: Pontefract Races Autism In Racing EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Anna Woolley Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Invincible Ruby
runners_data.note: Won over this C&D on good ground six days ago, making her the freshest winner in the field and the most natural closer; David Allan-style hold-up racing suits a small field but her recent course form makes her the standout finisher to watch.

runners_data.name: One Of Our Own
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who sets the entire shape of this race; worn tongue strap, trained by in-form Rebecca Menzies (1 from 25 last 14 days), and has won over this C&D on good ground — her ability to dictate unchallenged is the single biggest tactical factor.

runners_data.name: Lindoro
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose recent form reads 64-88 and whose only placed runs came on soft or good-to-soft; the good ground here and modest trainer strike rate (0 from 2 in 14 days) are mild concerns, and he has yet to show he can compete at this level.

runners_data.name: Ishe Worth Agamble
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for Tim Easterby who has placed in three of his last five and goes well on good ground at this trip; tongue strap in place, David Allan takes the ride which is a notable booking, and proximity to the pace suits today's shape.

runners_data.name: Maui Breeze
runners_data.note: Has run all his recent form over further (7f-10f) on soft or standard, and this drop to 6f on good ground represents a significant ask — Wilf Storey yard has had no runners in the last 14 days and there is no obvious angle here.

runners_data.name: Instant Bond
runners_data.note: Two wins in his last six starts, both on standard or soft, and his good-ground figures are modest; J F Egan takes the ride for a two-from-three trainer in the last 14 days, and he will race prominently, but the going could be an edge against him.

runners_data.name: He's An Angel
runners_data.note: Finished second last time out on good ground and has raw ability, but his best form is at 5f-6f on standard or soft; Kevin & Lauren Frost have been booking him consistently and he is a genuine closer by nature — pushed into a midfield slot today, the position compromises his effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Ideal Guest
runners_data.note: Harriet Bethell's seven-year-old hold-up horse whose placed form is mostly on soft ground over 7f; Sean D Bowen's jockey booking is interesting, but the good surface and drop to 6f are against him based on his form profile.

runners_data.name: Melissa Honey
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good ground last time and has strong recent form (8-6431); Daniel Tudhope is a major upgrade in the saddle and she has the pace profile to finish powerfully — by nature a closer, she finds herself racing closer to the pace than ideal today but Tudhope's hands make her dangerous regardless.

runners_data.name: So Grateful
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a form string of 9097-9 who goes well enough on good ground but rarely converts; by instinct a hold-up horse, in this deep field of closers he will be shuffled into midfield rather than his preferred berth, and his overall profile suggests a minor role at best.

runners_data.name: Diligent Henry
runners_data.note: Visor-wearing hold-up type whose form is almost entirely over 7f on tapeta or soft, making this 6f good-ground contest a significant step outside his comfort zone; Jessica Macey's yard has had no winners from nine runners in 14 days and there is no compelling reason to promote him.

runners_data.name: Ziva's Star
runners_data.note: Placed three times at 5f on good ground and has shown some ability, but her wider form (0-7793) and consistent midfield finishes suggest she needs things to go wrong around her to feature; by preference a closer, she too will find her natural position harder to secure in this crowded hold-up division.

races.paceDynamic: One Of Our Own is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 6f handicap at Pontefract, and on good ground she should be able to dictate at a sustainable, uncontested tempo without significant pressure from her rivals. Ishe Worth Agamble and Instant Bond will push forward to prominent positions behind her, creating a conventional lead-prominent shape rather than a contested pace battle. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — He's An Angel, Melissa Honey, So Grateful, Diligent Henry, and Ziva's Star are all genuine closers who cannot all settle at the rear and will be compressed into midfield, meaning their ability to find their true running style is compromised. With a single pace-setter controlling matters at a fair but not suicidal gallop, this race shape clearly favours horses who can race prominently or just off the pace and sustain their effort through the Pontefract dip and up the rise — a premium on relaxed, prominent-to-midfield types with proven good-ground speed, while the redistribution of multiple true hold-up horses into the midfield pack dulls the finish-end advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: One Of Our Own Controls
scenarios.trigger: If One Of Our Own leads from the front unchallenged and sets a fair, measured gallop that suits the prominent-to-midfield chasers.
scenarios.body: If One Of Our Own leads from the front unchallenged and sets a fair, measured gallop that suits the prominent-to-midfield chasers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If One Of Our Own sets only a modest pace that compresses the field and allows Ishe Worth Agamble and Instant Bond to challenge decisively turning for home.
scenarios.body: If One Of Our Own sets only a modest pace that compresses the field and allows Ishe Worth Agamble and Instant Bond to challenge decisively turning for home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply early and One Of Our Own over-extends herself, leaving those racing from off the pace with energy in reserve for the closing stages.
scenarios.body: If the pace quickens sharply early and One Of Our Own over-extends herself, leaving those racing from off the pace with energy in reserve for the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Frees Rebel
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves too strong even for One Of Our Own, creating a false-pace scenario where a recovering midfield runner steals the spoils.
scenarios.body: If the early pace proves too strong even for One Of Our Own, creating a false-pace scenario where a recovering midfield runner steals the spoils.

watchPoints.text: One Of Our Own is the sole pace-setter — if she is crowded or bumped at the start, the race loses its single tactical anchor and the entire scenario framework shifts toward a messy early contest.

Melissa Honey with Daniel Tudhope is a significant jockey upgrade; watch whether Tudhope elects to push forward early given the redistribution pressure on hold-up horses, which could either improve or disrupt her chance.

Invincible Ruby runs just six days after winning over this course and distance — watch market moves at the off; if her post-race welfare was perfect she is the most dangerous closer, but the short turnaround is a flag.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (He's An Angel, So Grateful, Diligent Henry, Ziva's Star) will fight for midfield positions in the early stages; any resulting traffic at the top of the straight on Pontefract's turning track could cause interference and benefit those racing prominently.

Ishe Worth Agamble and Instant Bond are both equipped with headgear (tongue straps) and have been consistently placed at this trip — watch their market as the race approaches; either could be the each-way play if their trainer/jockey form translates to the good surface.

races.name: Ponte Premiership Points Mean Prizes Handicap

runners_data.name: Goyard
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's stablemate — wait, David O'Meara's charge — returns after a lengthy 260-day absence and is the race's only mapped leader; his 1/5f/GOO win shows he handles this trip and going, but fitness after a 38-week break is a genuine concern that could blunt his chance at the business end.

runners_data.name: Hiya Maite
runners_data.note: Roy Bowring's veteran 8-year-old returns after 168 days off and carries stable form concerns (T14: 0/3), but has strong prominent-running credentials on soft and standard; limited Good-ground record (0W1P in 15 sim-going runs) tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Lethal Nymph
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley runner fresh from just 8 days ago and therefore race-fit; a 0W0P record in six similar-going runs is sobering, but she races prominently and the quick turnaround suggests she ran well enough last time to warrant another visit here.

runners_data.name: Reigning Profit
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's hold-up specialist has a 2-placed record in 15 similar-going runs and a genuine win on good, but from her natural rear position she needs a stronger pace than Goyard is likely to set; headgear (visor) adds a small behavioural wildcard.

runners_data.name: Dakota Gold
runners_data.note: A 12-year-old hold-up type who hasn't won since better days, with form figures of 20/9/5 in recent similar-going runs telling a story of declining competitiveness; Connor Beasley can't conjure finishing runs that simply aren't coming any more.

runners_data.name: Squealer
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's hold-up horse wears a hood and has a 1W3P record in 13 similar-going appearances, suggesting he can be competitive but needs strong pace to produce his late effort; that pace is unlikely to materialise, making his task harder than his handicap mark implies.

runners_data.name: Ventura Express
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan partnering a true rear-of-field type for Paul Midgley — though forced into a midfield map position by the congestion of hold-up horses in this field, his natural instinct to drop back means his actual finishing position could be further back still than the race map suggests.

runners_data.name: D Flawless
runners_data.note: Jason Hart's 5-year-old is an authentic hold-up performer whose sole win came at 6f on standard; pressed into a midfield role by the clustering of closers in this race, his best going record is modest (0W1P in 5 similar-going runs) and the style compromise is a meaningful handicap here.

runners_data.name: Equity Law
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's well-tried prominent racer is in the hands of David Allan and comes here just 10 days after his last start, suggesting bounce-back freshness; a 2W5P record in 12 similar-going runs is the best strike-rate among the prominent types and he handles 5f on good ground.

runners_data.name: South Parade
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's 5-year-old is a genuine back-of-the-field runner who has been pushed into the midfield map due to the hold-up traffic; his best form (4/5f/SOF) came on softer ground and recent Good-ground outings have produced 7th, 12th, and 12th — finishing position is the honest expectation.

races.paceDynamic: Goyard is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to press him from the gates, he should slot straight into an uncontested lead at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this sharp 5f on good ground at Pontefract. The prominent types — Hiya Maite, Lethal Nymph, and Equity Law — will sit just off his heels, creating an orderly early order rather than a scorching pace, which means the complexion of this race is set from the off with minimal friction. Ventura Express, D Flawless, and South Parade are true hold-up horses but the sheer weight of prominent/midfield runners means all three are redistributed toward the middle of the pack rather than their preferred rear positions, compromising their ability to deliver the sustained late surge their style demands. This race shape — a controlled pace set by one horse with prominent types tracking — strongly favours those who can race handily and quicken from just off the pace in the final two furlongs, rather than those needing a deep late run from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Goyard Controls, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Goyard dictates a steady-to-fair gallop unchallenged and the race sets up as a two-furlong dash from the front.
scenarios.body: If Goyard dictates a steady-to-fair gallop unchallenged and the race sets up as a two-furlong dash from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace causes a sprint-finish bunfight among the four or five horses racing prominently.
scenarios.body: If the moderate pace causes a sprint-finish bunfight among the four or five horses racing prominently.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Defies Position
scenarios.trigger: If a compressed, slow-run race produces a late gap that allows one redistributed horse to weave through on the inside rail.
scenarios.body: If a compressed, slow-run race produces a late gap that allows one redistributed horse to weave through on the inside rail.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Front Runner Exposed
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is higher than expected and Goyard is asked hard questions before the turn, weakening the lead entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the early gallop is higher than expected and Goyard is asked hard questions before the turn, weakening the lead entering the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Goyard's 260-day absence is a serious fitness flag — watch his pre-race condition and if he breaks sluggishly or fades sharply before the final furlong, the race could collapse quickly into a prominent-horse scramble benefiting Equity Law or Hiya Maite.

Ventura Express, D Flawless, and South Parade are all mapped out of their true hold-up position — if all three drift back to their natural rear berths in running, the midfield becomes dangerously compressed and finishing lanes on Pontefract's straight 5f will be fiercely contested.

Equity Law's Tim Easterby stable is in strong form (T14: 10/94) and the horse has the best similar-going placed record of any prominent type — watch for David Allan to hunt an early prominent pitch that could make the difference in a controlled pace scenario.

Reigning Profit's visor (hg:v) is worth noting for a hold-up horse who needs to switch off early — headgear changes at this level sometimes sharpen an older horse's finishing effort and she has placed twice on comparable good ground.

races.name: Pontefract Castle Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Ryka
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 4yo has won twice at 12f on Soft and once at 10f on Good, making this trip on Good ground a live angle; Tudhope rides and she has strong prominent form, giving her a natural role tracking Coedana from a good position.

runners_data.name: Brielle
runners_data.note: Won last time at 12f on Good in a confidence-boosting return but is a natural front-runner/prominent type who will find herself shuffled into midfield given the congestion of pace horses here, making her task harder than her form figure suggests.

runners_data.name: Cabrera
runners_data.note: Headgear noted (p), and has shown best form on quicker ground around 12f, but is another genuine prominently-run horse who cannot realistically hold that position in this field and must race off the pace against her instincts — temper expectations accordingly.

runners_data.name: Coedana
runners_data.note: OR=103 and the confirmed lone front runner here; has form on Soft but her best Pontefract-level form has come on Stable ground, and with no pressure she controls the pace entirely — the open question is whether she has the reserves to hold on when challenged from two out.

runners_data.name: Ghaiyya
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's filly has four wins on Good going and genuine form at this trip, but like Brielle and Cabrera she is a naturally prominent type who must cede that spot to Coedana and find herself racing further back than ideal — four wins on Good does keep her in the picture if she adapts.

runners_data.name: Lemsairbat
runners_data.note: O'Brien's 5yo hold-up mare has placed five times in recent starts without winning; she is a true hold-up type whose chance depends on a genuinely honest pace from Coedana stretching the field, and her step up from 10f to 12f last time was not encouraging.

runners_data.name: Little Dorrit
runners_data.note: 268 days off the track is the dominant factor here for Roger Varian's 3yo; she has won at Listed level and holds Good-ground form, but the extended absence means fitness is unproven, and hold-up horses returning after nine months face a steep ask against seasoned rivals.

runners_data.name: Merveilleux Lapin
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows's 4yo has placed at this trip on Good and is a genuine hold-up type; only one run on Good in her recent hist limits the going confidence, but she has placed twice at 10f on Good and her Callum Rodriguez booking keeps her relevant in a scenario where the pace is truly honest.

runners_data.name: Revoir
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's 4yo has placed consistently at this grade but has not won since dropping to OR=101 territory; headgear noted (p), runs prominent but has zero wins in five recent starts — her finishing kick is real but she needs a true pace to expose rivals, and a controlled tempo suits those ahead of her.

races.paceDynamic: Coedana is the confirmed front runner and, with no genuine challenger willing to push her for the lead, she will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over this 1m4f trip on Good ground at Pontefract. Ryka and Orionis are the most likely to travel prominently behind her, tracking the leader through the early stages and positioning themselves to strike approaching the straight. This field contains more pace-inclined horses than can realistically secure their natural berth — Ghaiyya, Brielle, and Cabrera all want to race prominently but will be shuffled into midfield positions against their instincts, compromising their effectiveness. With one horse dictating an honest but uncontested gallop, the race shape strongly favours genuine prominent horses who can track Coedana and produce a sustained finish, or high-class hold-up types with the engine to close from a realistic position — not the redistribution midfielders, who are operating out of role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Coedana Controls, Tracked Danger
scenarios.trigger: If Coedana sets a controlled front-running pace and the race unfolds at a steady-to-honest tempo with prominent trackers poised.
scenarios.body: If Coedana sets a controlled front-running pace and the race unfolds at a steady-to-honest tempo with prominent trackers poised.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Late Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo proves genuinely honest and the closers get enough cover to produce their finishing kick late.
scenarios.body: If the tempo proves genuinely honest and the closers get enough cover to produce their finishing kick late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Coedana is entirely unchallenged and the gallop is too slow for closers to organise a meaningful challenge.
scenarios.body: If Coedana is entirely unchallenged and the gallop is too slow for closers to organise a meaningful challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Open Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the jostling for position among the pace-heavy field creates a messy early race with no settled rhythm.
scenarios.body: If the jostling for position among the pace-heavy field creates a messy early race with no settled rhythm.

watchPoints.text: Orionis is the standout prominent tracker to watch — Haggas in form, Marquand booked, won at 12f on Good last time, and she occupies the position that suits her naturally behind Coedana while redistributed rivals cannot.

Ghaiyya, Brielle, and Cabrera will all be fighting for positions that only one horse can realistically hold behind Coedana — watch for congestion and shuffling in the early stages that could compromise all three.

Coedana faces a stamina test if she sets even a modest pace alone for 1m4f on Good — watch for signs of her weakening inside the final two furlongs if she has been unable to conserve enough through the early stages.

Little Dorrit's 268-day absence is significant — watch her in the paddock and early in the race for any signs that the layoff has blunted her sharpness, particularly over this trip where fitness is paramount.

Lemsairbat's chance is entirely conditional on tempo — if Coedana's sectionals in the first half of the race are slow, closers including Lemsairbat and Merveilleux Lapin will find the front two gone too far to close.

races.name: Moor Top Farm Shop Hemsworth Pontefract Cup Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Sax Appeal
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner in the field who will be gifted an uncontested lead by Beasley; six-year-old with a patchy recent record (no win or place on similar going in last 15 outings) suggests he may be vulnerable to being reeled in once the field turns for home despite his tactical advantage.

runners_data.name: Anzac Day
runners_data.note: Returning from a lengthy 285-day layoff (30 jumps runs interpolated) for Jonjo & A J O'Neill, who are on a cold 0/12 in the last 14 days; the extended absence and trainer form combine to make this a speculative reappearance, and his best form has come over shorter trips on Good ground.

runners_data.name: Trojan Soldier
runners_data.note: Four-year-old in explosive form — three wins from his last four starts including back-to-back victories — and Jack Garritty's booking for Jedd O'Keeffe (1/8 T14) gives this a live angle; hold-up style suits a race likely to be run at a controlled pace, and his sim-going record of 1W3P from 12 similar-going runs underlines course-type suitability.

runners_data.name: Secret Force
runners_data.note: Races prominently for Adrian Keatley and returns quickly after just eight days, fitted with a tongue-tie; best recent form has come over shorter distances (11-12f), and stepping up markedly to 2m2f on this evidence represents an unexplored stamina question that is hard to dismiss.

runners_data.name: Isle Of Sark
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old with a deep record over marathon trips and an excellent sim-going profile (2W6P from 15 similar-ground runs); a genuine hold-up horse by nature, he is displaced to midfield on the map because the field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — his chance depends on Jack Nicholls (5) finding a clear run from whatever position he settles.

runners_data.name: Treasure Islands
runners_data.note: Recent course-and-distance form is compelling — a win over 16f on Good ground and placed efforts bookending it — and David Allan knows this horse well; by inclination a prominent racer, it is shown in midfield on the map because the field cannot hold all prominent types in that position, though Allan is likely to push forward early and reclaim closer ground than the map suggests.

races.paceDynamic: Sax Appeal is the lone confirmed front-runner in a six-horse field over 2m2f at Pontefract on Good ground, and with no genuine rival to challenge for the lead, Connor Beasley can dictate a controlled, energy-efficient tempo from the front. That sustainable pace is the defining feature of this race shape — no pressure means the race is likely to be run at a rhythm that suits whoever can travel fluently and quicken, rather than those who rely on a true test of stamina developed by a searching gallop. Trojan Sand and Secret Force both have prominent tendencies but neither is a natural front-runner, meaning Sax Appeal is almost certain to enjoy an uncontested lead throughout. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a sharp finishing kick over pure stayers, provided they can close on a front-runner who has been allowed to coast — the field contains more prominent and hold-up types than the map can cleanly place, with Treasure Islands and Isle Of Sark both true to their natural styles but displaced to midfield on the map; in practice, Treasure Islands is the more likely of the two to push forward and secure a position closer to the pace given its genuine prominent inclination.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sax Appeal Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Sax Appeal bowls clear from the off and no rival applies early pressure, allowing Beasley to set a measured, controlled tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: If Sax Appeal bowls clear from the off and no rival applies early pressure, allowing Beasley to set a measured, controlled tempo throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Sax Appeal sets a truly dawdling pace that gifts hold-up horses an easy opportunity to close with one sweeping run from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If Sax Appeal sets a truly dawdling pace that gifts hold-up horses an easy opportunity to close with one sweeping run from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Picks Up Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent types forces the tempo earlier than expected, turning this into a genuine test of stamina rather than a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: If one of the prominent types forces the tempo earlier than expected, turning this into a genuine test of stamina rather than a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Scrappy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If positional jostling and a lack of early order creates a muddling race with no one horse controlling the shape.
scenarios.body: If positional jostling and a lack of early order creates a muddling race with no one horse controlling the shape.

watchPoints.text: Trojan Soldier's three-race winning streak combined with his hold-up style ideally suited to a Sax Appeal-led dawdle makes him the horse most likely to close late and decisively — watch for Garritty to track the leader from mid-race.

Sax Appeal's complete absence of a win or place on similar going in 15 attempts is a significant red flag; if Beasley cannot quicken clear in the straight after dictating, the field will swamp him before the line.

Treasure Islands' natural urge to race prominently means David Allan may push forward despite the map showing midfield — if it ends up racing closer than expected it could complicate the pace picture and compress the gaps for hold-up horses.

Anzac Day's 285-day absence and trainer's poor 14-day record (0/12) make him a significant unknown quantity; watch in the paddock and early in the race for signs of ring-rustiness that could cause interference in this small field.

Isle Of Sark's tongue-tie and strong course-type record (11/15 sim-going) make him one to monitor for market support — if Jack Nicholls (5) can navigate a clean run from the pack, his proven stamina is a live factor at the business end.

races.name: Sunpak Potatoes Handicap

runners_data.name: Badri
runners_data.note: Recent 6f Good win is the key form line; Michael Herrington's yard is running at 2/16 over 14 days, modest but not alarming; at age 9 he is best when allowed to stride on unchallenged, but his STYLE_FIT tag warns that any disruption to his front-running role materially reduces his chance.

runners_data.name: Russet Gold
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's six-year-old has zero wins or places from seven Good or similar-ground runs, which is a damning statistic on today's surface; Tom Eaves rides but the hold-up style demands more pace than Badri is likely to generate in a small, lightly-pressured field.

runners_data.name: Ray Mon Dough
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with an unconventional style profile whose sole win came over this exact trip and surface; Tom Marquand is a major booking for Oliver Cole's yard, and the 34-day absence is not a concern for a lightly-raced type; headgear flag worth noting for a horse still learning its trade.

runners_data.name: The Good Biscuit
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners a mare with a superbly consistent Pontefract profile — four of her last five runs have come on Good 6f and she has placed in three of them; Ruth Carr sends her out fresh at 19 days, and her prominent style slots neatly into the dominant race shape.

runners_data.name: Azure Zain
runners_data.note: Most recent run produced a 6f Good win and she has a solid similar-going record (1W2P from four runs); the 43-day break is slightly longer than ideal, and Warren Fentiman's claim could be an asset at the weights, though the hold-up style relies on a stronger gallop than this race is likely to offer.

runners_data.name: Rock Opera
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr takes over for Fahey's yard, which has been notably busy (5/52 over 14 days, strong strike rate); Rock Opera's last three runs have all been on Good 6f and include a win and two places — the form underpins his chance as the most profile-consistent horse in the race for the dominant scenario.

runners_data.name: Mister Sox
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's veteran is a genuine front-runner in terms of racing style; the pace map has pushed him to midfield because prominent slots are already occupied, meaning he races out of role and carries a STYLE_FIT discount — his recent form figures of 02870 also give little encouragement, though the switch to headgear (p) is a small positive flag.

races.paceDynamic: Badri is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only Rock Opera and The Good Biscuit as genuine prominent types to press, shapes up to control this 6f at a sustainable, unexploited tempo on Good ground. Mister Sox is a natural front-runner in reality but has been mapped to midfield because the prominent berths are already contested — he is unlikely to secure his preferred pitch, which dilutes his chance in a pace-led shape. With Badri able to bowl along unchallenged or only lightly pressed, the race is set up to be run at an honest but not brutal gallop, which historically suits horses that can travel prominently or just off the pace rather than deep hold-up types. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent-to-midfield racers who can latch onto Badri's controlled pace and quicken in the final furlong are best served by this shape, while genuine closers like Russet Gold and Azure Zain will need more pace to run into than this field is likely to generate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Badri Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Badri leads unchallenged and sets an honest but sustainable gallop, allowing a prominent tracker to pounce.
scenarios.body: If Badri leads unchallenged and sets an honest but sustainable gallop, allowing a prominent tracker to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Badri Pinches It Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If no rival picks up the challenge and the early tempo is genuinely modest, allowing Badri to steal an uncontested lead and hold on.
scenarios.body: If no rival picks up the challenge and the early tempo is genuinely modest, allowing Badri to steal an uncontested lead and hold on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses collectively set a stronger pace than expected, opening the race up for closers to finish through.
scenarios.body: If the prominent horses collectively set a stronger pace than expected, opening the race up for closers to finish through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Mister Sox Bounces Back
scenarios.trigger: If early crowding or a slow break disrupts the prominent brigade and Mister Sox finds an uncontested rail run from his mapped midfield position.
scenarios.body: If early crowding or a slow break disrupts the prominent brigade and Mister Sox finds an uncontested rail run from his mapped midfield position.

watchPoints.text: Rock Opera has produced a win and two places from his last three 6f Good runs and Oisin Orr's booking for an in-form Fahey yard makes him the most dangerous prominent tracker if Badri leads at a sustainable pace.

Azure Zain's 43-day absence is the longest in the field — watch the market moves for signals that Fahey has her cherry-ripe, as a forward show in the ring would upgrade her hold-up chance significantly.

Mister Sox is a natural front-runner squeezed into midfield by the pace map — if he pushes forward early and upsets the expected order, the whole race shape could compress and disadvantage the late movers.

The Good Biscuit has placed in three of her last five 6f Good runs at this course and is the most consistent horse in the field on the surface — any market support for Joanna Mason's mount should be respected given the track-specific form.

Ray Mon Dough is the only three-year-old in the race and carries a headgear flag — an unexposed profile with Tom Marquand aboard means he could outrun his odds if the race unfolds at a manageable tempo that suits his developing style.

runners_data.name: Amidst The Chaos

runners_data.name: Ravishing Beauty

runners_data.note: Prominent-running 4yo trained by Richard Hannon who has struggled on Tapeta recently but returns to turf on Good ground where his single placed effort came; Alec Voikhansky rides and the horse has nine runs without a win recently, making confidence limited.|

runners_data.note: Consistent 6yo with genuine hold-up tendencies who carries tongue strap for Tim Easterby; with the rear of the field congested, he is likely to race further forward than ideal — his best chance emerges only if the pace collapse scenario materialises, which the current setup makes unlikely.|

runners_data.name: Thats My Boy Luke
runners_data.note: Wears a hood for Tim Easterby and has a hold-up profile that sits awkwardly in a slow-run race; like stablemate Mount King, the overcrowding at the back forces him into a midfield berth he wouldn't naturally seek, and recent form figures of 58-470 offer little confidence.|

runners_data.name: Masaban
runners_data.note: The key pace influence: Edward Bethell's 3yo won at 8f on Good last time out and Connor Beasley will dictate the tempo from the front; Good ground is fine, and with no rival capable of seriously disputing, he could control this throughout — the STYLE_FIT flag notes he is mapped as prominent/quasi-lead which is broadly accurate.|

runners_data.name: Keep An Eye On It
runners_data.note: Unexposed 3yo from Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood partnership, returning after 70 days which is the biggest layoff in the field; Tom Marquand is a quality booking and the horse has shown ability at this trip on Good, but the freshness query and steady pace scenario make it hard to land from a hold-up position.|

runners_data.name: Kiss For An Angel
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey 3yo whose best effort was a 2nd at 8f on Good, which is relevant form, but she has since run 10th and 9th and the hold-up profile is poorly suited to Masaban's likely pace control; Barry McHugh rides and the step back to a mile is the one positive trigger.|

races.paceDynamic: Masaban is the single confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine pace rival likely to dispute the lead, Connor Beasley can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits the horse on Good ground around Pontefract's mile. That controlled, uncontested lead sets up a race that is likely to be run at a measured gallop, rewarding those travelling prominently rather than those hunting down a strong pace from the rear. Ravishing Beauty and Gennadius are the natural prominent challengers who will sit just off Masaban and be best placed to exploit a steady-run race, while the hold-up types — Amidst The Chaos, Kiss For An Angel, and Keep An Eye On It — face a stiff task to close ground if the pace never truly tests the leader. The field holds more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the back: Mount King and Thats My Boy Luke are genuine hold-up types but are mapped to midfield as the rear positions are oversold, meaning both race out of their natural role and their effectiveness is compromised. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently and travel smoothly into the straight, as the lone front-runner is unlikely to be pressured into collapse.

watchPoints.text: Watch Masaban's early position: if Beasley elects to go forward hard from the stalls, he sets a controlling lead; if anything delays him, Ravishing Beauty or Gennadius could end up in front and fundamentally alter the pace scenario.

Mount King and Thats My Boy Luke are both Tim Easterby hold-up horses likely to race out of their preferred style in this shape — if David Allan or Jason Hart drop them in behind a slow pace, they face a near-impossible task closing ground on the leader.

Keep An Eye On It is 70 days off the track, the longest absence in the field — monitor market moves on course as a market drift would confirm connections are treating this as a pipe-opener rather than a winning mission.
Ravishing Beauty's trainer Jedd O'Keeffe has a 1/1 record in the past 14 days — a sharp stable form angle worth noting given how well-placed she should be tactically in this race shape.
